Our client is a leading international renewable energy business specializing in the development of utility-scale solar power projects. By delivering intelligent and sustainable solutions, they generate clean, reliable electricity for homes and businesses across Europe and beyond. Committed to a green future, they foster a fast-paced, collaborative, and innovative working environment.

The I&C Contact Coordinator takes end-to-end ownership of booking and managing metering appointments for Industrial & Commercial (I&C) customers. - Query Resolution: Manage, track, and resolve operational queries through the internal company query portal in line with agreed processes and SLAs.
- H&S Support: Handle and log environmental, health, and safety incident calls directly from field operatives under the company's emergency reporting protocols.
- Stakeholder Collaboration: Resolve internal and external stakeholder queries and escalations using effective written and verbal communication, working collaboratively across operational teams.
- Performance & Data Integrity: Consistently meet performance targets (SLAs/KPIs) set by the Team Leader while maintaining high levels of accuracy and attention to detail in data entry across multiple internal systems.
- Administrative Support: Prioritize workload effectively to manage competing deadlines, providing flexible support for specialist campaigns and administrative activities as required.

Key Behaviours
- Customer-First Mindset: Professional, confident, and calm under pressure, with a passion for delivering excellent customer service.
- Team Player: A supportive colleague with a flexible, positive attitude who willingly shares knowledge to boost team performance.
- Results-Driven: Highly organized, target-driven, and focused on getting things "right first time" while working responsibly without close supervision.
- Continuous Improvement: Proactively reflects on personal performance and participates in regular training to develop skills.

Communication & Interpersonal Skills
- Excellent telephone manner with articulate, clear verbal communication skills.
- Strong listening skills with the ability to build rapport and understand customer/colleague needs.
- Precise and professional written communication skills for email correspondence.

Technical Skills & Knowledge
- Strong administrative and organizational capabilities with a keen eye for detail.
- Proven problem-solving and analytical abilities.
- Confident and accurate in utilizing departmental computer systems and databases.
- IT Literacy: Intermediate proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, and Outlook).

title: Credit Controller
description:
Are you a confident Credit Controller who knows how to navigate the world of council payments and gaining invoice payment from local authorities? If you understand the complexities of the public sector payment process and have the persistence to turn outstanding invoices into cash, this could be the opportunity you've been waiting for!
We're working with a successful and growing business looking for an experienced Credit Controller to take ownership of outstanding debt, build strong relationships with councils and keep cash flowing in the right direction.
What's the role all about?
This isn't just about sending statements and chasing overdue invoices. You'll play a key role in managing the company's debtor ledger, with a particular focus on collecting outstanding payments from councils, local authorities and other public sector organisations.
You'll need to be comfortable navigating complex payment processes, dealing with multiple stakeholders and understanding why public sector invoices can sometimes take longer than expected to settle. Managing and reducing aged debt across a portfolio of customer accounts.

Investigating payment delays, resolving invoice queries and addressing discrepancies.
Building effective working relationships with finance teams and accounts payable departments.
Reconciling customer accounts and allocating payments accurately.
Monitoring credit limits, identifying potential risks and escalating problem accounts.
Producing regular aged debt reports and providing updates on collection performance.
Working closely with internal finance and operational teams to resolve issues quickly.
What are we looking for?
You'll already have experience in a credit control role, ideally with demonstrable success collecting debt from councils, local authorities or wider public sector organisations.
You'll be an excellent communicator, highly organised and resilient enough to keep chasing when payments don't arrive as expected. You'll also have a keen eye for detail, strong reconciliation skills and the confidence to manage difficult conversations professionally.
If you enjoy taking ownership, solving problems and seeing the tangible results of your efforts, this role offers the chance to make a real difference to cash flow and working capital.
If you know your way around public sector debt collection and are ready for your next challenge, we'd love to hear from you.
